title_zh: 都市爱情剧：屋顶上的夕阳
title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (2/20): Sunset on the Rooftop
note_en: 先……后来…… marks a sequence of stages: 先是因为误会而争吵，后来却渐渐产生感情 "first they quarrel over a misunderstanding, but later they gradually fall for each other." 先 sits right before the verb (先是...), while 后来 opens the next clause; the verbs themselves never change form, since Chinese has no past tense to show the order of events.

sentences.en: She said that one of the most common male leads in urban romance is the "domineering CEO" (badao zongcai): usually successful and forceful, he gradually becomes gentle and caring around the heroine. Because the plot is fairly predictable, many viewers watch at double speed just to get to the couple's sweet scenes faster.

sentences.en: Xiao Min said that besides sweet romances, urban love stories can also be divided into subgenres such as campus romance and workplace romance. The Best of Us, for instance, is about the innocent, half-understood feelings between two high school deskmates, while Ode to Joy places its love stories within the working lives and friendships of women in the city.

sentences.en: She also said that another common trope in urban romance is "marriage first, love later," in which the leads marry for practical reasons and only slowly develop feelings while living together. Chinese audiences also generally prefer a happy ending, and if a show unusually ends in tragedy, it often sparks fierce debate online.

sentences.en: She said that for an urban romance, the on-screen chemistry between the leads is often more important than the script itself. A pairing that audiences feel "really works" can even boost both actors' popularity and commercial value, so producers pay particular attention to the chemistry between the two when casting.
